title: The parts desk that couldn't find HX-4410
scenario:
You are a product manager at an industrial equipment wholesaler. The sales desk answers questions from customers about 60,000 parts. A pilot assistant searches the product catalogue and the FAQ pages, then writes an answer.

The sales director is unhappy with the pilot and wants a decision this week. The exhibit shows the pilot report.
exhibit:
Parts desk assistant: pilot report (made-up example data)

Knowledge base: product catalogue (38,000 pages) + FAQ (250 pages)
Search: meaning-based (embeddings) only, top 10 chunks per question

Test set: 200 real sales-desk questions
  Type                              Count  Right passage found  Answer correct
  By meaning ("pump for salt water")  120          106                101
  By exact code ("HX-4410 in stock?")  80           34                 31
  Total                               200          140                132

The 68 wrong answers
  Right passage not found              60
  Right passage found, answer wrong     8

Draft cost line
  "Storage: 6 GB x $0.10 = $0.60 a day. That is the full running cost."

questions.prompt: The director asks: "Why not put the whole catalogue in every prompt and skip search?" What is the best answer?

options.text: Agree: the whole prompt is simplest, and prompt caching makes it cheap at any size.
options.explanation: Anthropic's post gives about 500 pages (200,000 tokens) as a rule of thumb (Sept 2024) for that approach. Caching helps cost, but it doesn't make 38,000 pages fit.

options.text: Disagree: 38,000 pages is far above the ~500 pages where the whole-prompt option fits.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's post (Sept 2024) gives a rule of thumb: the whole-prompt option below 200,000 tokens, about 500 pages. Far above that, retrieval is the typical solution.

options.text: Agree, but split the catalogue across ten prompts, then merge the ten answers afterwards.
options.explanation: Each prompt would still hold about 3,800 pages, far above the ~500-page guide, and merging ten answers adds new errors.

options.text: Disagree: keep only the 250 FAQ pages and drop the catalogue from the assistant.
options.explanation: The FAQ can't answer stock or code questions about specific parts, which are 80 of the 200 test questions.

questions.prompt: Exact-code questions found the right passage 34 times out of 80. What change fits the sources best?

options.text: Fine-tune the model on part codes, so that it learns every code in the catalogue.
options.explanation: The failure is in search: the passage never reaches the model. Fine-tuning changes the model, not what search returns.

options.text: Raise the chunks per question from 10 to 50, so the right code is more likely to appear.
options.explanation: More chunks found by meaning still miss exact codes, and OpenAI's accuracy guide warns that too much irrelevant context drowns out the real information.

options.text: Add keyword search, such as BM25, next to meaning search, so exact codes are matched.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's post says embeddings can miss exact matches like "TS-999" and that combining them with BM25 worked better than embeddings alone.

options.text: Ask staff to rephrase code questions in words, describing the part instead of its code.
options.explanation: Customers ask by code, and staff would lose time rewriting every question. The search should handle codes.

questions.prompt: Where should the team spend its effort first?

options.text: On retrieval: in 60 of the 68 wrong answers, the right passage never reached the model.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's accuracy guide splits RAG failures into retrieval and model problems. Here retrieval causes most of them.

options.text: On the prompt: the 68 wrong answers show that the model misreads the passages it receives.
options.explanation: Only 8 wrong answers had the right passage. The other 60 never gave the model a chance.

options.text: On the model: switch to a larger model, because 132 correct out of 200 is too low.
options.explanation: A larger model can't answer from a passage it never receives. The exhibit points to search.

options.text: On nothing yet: roll out now and collect complaints to learn which answers are wrong.
options.explanation: The test set already shows where it fails: 60 of 68 wrong answers come from search. Real customers would get those wrong answers.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the draft cost line? (OpenAI prices, checked 2026-10-06.)

options.text: Nothing: for a hosted search tool, storage is the only cost that the company pays.
options.explanation: OpenAI's pricing page also charges per file search call and bills the tokens the tool uses at model rates.

options.text: It is too high: storage is free for every vector store that is smaller than 10 GB.
options.explanation: The free amount is 1 GB across all stores, not 10 GB per store.

options.text: The storage maths is right, but the $0.10 rate is per month, so it should be lower.
options.explanation: OpenAI's guide prices storage per GB per day, so the rate is a daily one.

options.text: Two errors: 1 GB is free, so $0.50 a day; tool calls and tokens are also charged.
options.explanation: Right. (6 − 1) × $0.10 = $0.50 a day for storage. The pricing page adds $2.50 per 1,000 file search calls, plus tokens at model rates.
